Q1: What default should `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED` have in `mark-stable.yml` (lines 933/936) and `test-and-mark-stable.yml` (lines 6622/6625)?
Choices:
A) Default off, as the issue asks. Change `vars.RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED || 'true'` to `|| 'false'` and `${RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED-true}` to `-false`. Treat an empty or unset value as off, and only `true` (any letter case) as on. Update the step comments, README.md, the #7029 changelog wording through a new fragment, and `tests/test_release_validate_ci_gate.py` (`SWITCH_ENV`, the unset/empty cases). No stable tag, GitHub Release or consumer dispatch happens until someone sets the repo variable `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED=true`. The release jobs still end green with the "publishing disabled" summary.
B) Keep it default on, as #7029 intended (an off switch backed by the `CI / lint` gate). Close this activation gap as a false positive and change no workflow or test. At most, add a changelog/agents.d note recording that default-on is intentional. (RECOMMENDED)
C) Default off, and also keep `auto-release-stable.yml` from re-dispatching the gate while tagging is off (skip with a log line). This goes beyond what the issue asks.
**Note:** A and C stop all stable releases until a person sets the variable. With B the code does not change at all.
